topicDecisions.title: Northern Idaho — early Holocene
topicDecisions.status: screened; see admitted findings and held interpretations
topicDecisions.reviewFlags: Separate BP from cal BP and distinct occupation episodes. Older Cooper’s Ferry component dates must not overwrite the existing Area B model. A long site sequence does not establish continuous residence.

topicDecisions.title: Northern Nevada and Idaho — named sites
topicDecisions.status: screened; see admitted findings and held interpretations
topicDecisions.reviewFlags: Differentiate dated activity/cache evidence from habitation. Never use insect-cache or artifact counts as human population. Check revised Leonard Rockshelter chronology and explicit calibration.

topicDecisions.title: Aleutian occupation history
topicDecisions.status: screened; see admitted findings and held interpretations
topicDecisions.reviewFlags: The report headline extends residence across 10,000 BCE–1300 CE, but its body describes approximately 9,000-year-old earliest sites. Do not assign the query start as an occupation date or equate historical cranial categories with discrete migrating peoples.

topicDecisions.title: Individual Aleutian archaeological sites
topicDecisions.status: screened; see admitted findings and held interpretations
topicDecisions.reviewFlags: Verify individual dating, location precision and continuity claims. The existing Alaska rectangle starts at 54°N and misses much of the chain; compare both sides of the dateline before measuring this gap.

topicDecisions.title: Kiribati settlement and contacts
topicDecisions.status: screened; see admitted findings and held interpretations
topicDecisions.reviewFlags: Do not apply one arrival date across all island groups. Island emergence is not human settlement, and broad Micronesian ancestry is not a dated local occupation. Current Marshall/Kiribati audit bounds omit islands east of the dateline.

topicDecisions.title: Nuku Hiva and nearby Marquesan islands
topicDecisions.status: screened; see admitted findings and held interpretations
topicDecisions.reviewFlags: Retain dating disagreements and distinguish initial activity, settlement and sustained occupation. Check the reported Ho‘oumi 1129–1212 cal CE window against its original publication.

topicDecisions.title: Hawaiʻi settlement, trade and cultural development
topicDecisions.status: screened; see admitted findings and held interpretations
topicDecisions.reviewFlags: Keep competing arrival chronologies and source-specific date bounds; do not infer a single origin island or a precise cessation of voyaging.

topicDecisions.title: Hawaiian raiding and kingdom consolidation
topicDecisions.status: screened; see admitted findings and held interpretations
topicDecisions.reviewFlags: Resource stress is a proposed causal explanation, not automatically demonstrated. Repair missing-author citations and distinguish conquest, alliance and negotiated submission.

topicDecisions.title: Hawaiian political institutions and state formation
topicDecisions.status: screened; see admitted findings and held interpretations
topicDecisions.reviewFlags: Do not project later states backward or turn a conceptual pathway into a single dated event. Check temple, agricultural and warfare chronologies separately.

topicDecisions.title: Alaska, Yukon and northern Canadian Arctic
topicDecisions.status: screened; see admitted findings and held interpretations
topicDecisions.reviewFlags: Separate interior histories from coastal dispersals; show disputed early evidence and differing migration chronologies. Genetics, archaeological traditions and language affiliation need independent support.

topicDecisions.title: Inca report — exact repeat
topicDecisions.status: screened; see admitted findings and held interpretations
topicDecisions.reviewFlags: Revisit only for an unresolved original-source lead; do not duplicate existing round9 records.

topicDecisions.title: Louisiana — Poverty Point, Tchefuncte and Marksville
